name: Da Lat
provinceNote: Lam Dong now also includes the former Dak Nong and Binh Thuan provinces, so Mui Ne shares the province on paper.
dotReason: Worth a special trip in this corridor
summary: Sleep by Xuan Huong Lake when you want cool air, pine ridges, and a market slope of strawberries. Fly into Lien Khuong or bus up from Ho Chi Minh City. Go to Nha Trang or Mui Ne when the beach is the trip; they are still hours apart by road.
fee: The lake is free; palaces, gardens, and waterfalls ticket separately
getThere: Lien Khuong Airport (DLI), about 30 km south of town, with flights from Ha Noi and Ho Chi Minh City
seoTitle: Da Lat travel guide — lake, market, and cool highlands
seoDescription: Xuan Huong Lake, the market slope, and pine-country waterfalls. Lien Khuong is about 30 km south. December to March is the driest window.
intro: Wake to mist on Xuan Huong Lake and air cool enough for a jacket while the coast is hot. The shore walk and Lam Vien Square are the morning; the sloping market above the lake is strawberries, flowers, and avocado ice cream before lunch.

Stay if the highlands are the trip. Book Nha Trang or Mui Ne when you wanted sand. They share a province on paper after the merger and they are still a long ride apart, so link them from Ho Chi Minh City rather than in one afternoon.

Give a southbound half-day to the cable car from Robin Hill, Truc Lam monastery, and Tuyen Lam Lake, or to Datanla Falls on Prenn Pass. Lang Biang is the northbound half-day. Crazy House and Bao Dai Palace III fit between lake mornings. The tourist railway station is the art-deco run toward mosaic-covered Linh Phuoc at Trai Mat.

After dark the night market lanes grill rice paper and pour hot soy milk while the lake path stays lit. The 11th Flower Festival in 2026 opens at Lam Vien Square on 19 December and closes on 31 December, with displays into early January. Odd-year December is the pattern; confirm the next year on arrival.
gettingAround: Lien Khuong Airport is about 30 km south on National Highway 20. Vietnam Tourism names flights from Ha Noi and Ho Chi Minh City; the road minutes and taxi fare are check on arrival. In town, walk the lake and market, and use Grab or a taxi for Prenn Pass, Lang Biang, and Trai Mat. Easy-rider motorbike loops to waterfalls are common; ride yourself only with the proper license.

stayAreas.name: Around Xuan Huong Lake
stayAreas.summary: Walk to the market, Lam Vien Square, and the evening lake path.

stayAreas.name: Pine ridges
stayAreas.summary: Quieter beds above the basin with valley views. No hotel street is published as a pick.

eat: Morning is the market slope: strawberries with condensed milk, artichoke tea souvenirs, and banh mi from a counter. Evening is the night market for banh trang nuong and soy milk. Coffee belongs to the hills around Cau Dat; the food guide names areas, not shops.
interestsBody: Dining is market strawberries, kem bo, and night-market rice paper. The food guide is photo-led.
Coffee is Arabica country on the Cau Dat hills and slow cups after the lake walk. Farm names on Vietnam Tourism are tours, not picks.
Lakes and waterfalls are Xuan Huong in town, then Tuyen Lam, Datanla, and Lang Biang on half-day rides.
French hill-station architecture is the railway station, Bao Dai Palace III, the Chicken Church, Domaine de Marie, and Crazy House.
Flowers are Lam Vien Square and the December festival displays around the lake in odd years. The ticketed city flower garden has no licensed card photo in this pass.
Cool evenings are the night market and the lakeside walk, not a beach-bar strip.

blocks.heading: Da Lat Market
paragraphs: The Vietnam Tourism Da Lat page says the stalls of the central market are packed with fresh flowers and colourful produce. The sight page adds strawberries in the sloping halls, and it says the door is free. Walk uphill from Xuan Huong Lake.

The address and the hours were not on the provincial market page when it was opened. Both are check on arrival. Stall prices are check on arrival. The night stalls the sight page puts after 18:00 are the food walk, not a second card here.

cards.title: Da Lat Market
cards.summary: Fresh flowers and colourful produce on the Vietnam Tourism page, and strawberries on the sight page. The door is free. The address and the hours are check on arrival.

interestGroups.title: Coffee hills
interestGroups.summary: Arabica on the Cau Dat hills, and a slow cup after the lake. The food guide names areas, not a shop to cross town for.
body: Coffee belongs to the hills around Cau Dat. Vietnam Tourism names farm tours. Those names are tours, not picks, and no stall price is published.
The cup itself is the coffee page. Market strawberries and the night-market rice paper stay on the Da Lat food guide.

cards.title: Coffee hills
cards.summary: Cau Dat slopes and farm tours. No stall price is published. Drink it after the lake walk, not as a ranked cafe list.

interestGroups.title: Lakes and waterfalls
interestGroups.summary: Xuan Huong is the lake in town. Tuyen Lam, Truc Lam, and Datanla are the southbound half-day.

blocks.heading: The lake in town
paragraphs: Wake to mist on Xuan Huong and walk the shore. The lake is free. Palaces, gardens, and waterfalls ticket separately.

blocks.heading: South of town
paragraphs: Give a southbound half-day to the cable car from Robin Hill, Truc Lam monastery, and Tuyen Lam Lake, or to Datanla Falls on Prenn Pass. Lang Biang is the northbound half-day, and it has no licensed photograph here, so it is not a card.

cards.title: Xuan Huong Lake
cards.summary: The city lake for a walk, a pedal boat, or a cool evening loop. Bring a layer from November to January.

cards.title: Tuyen Lam Lake
cards.summary: The gate above the reservoir, with the water through the arch. Boating here is south of town, and it is not the same outing as Xuan Huong.

cards.title: Truc Lam
cards.summary: Zen monastery gardens above Tuyen Lam, usually reached by cable car.

cards.title: Datanla Falls
cards.summary: Waterfall on Prenn Pass with optional coaster or guided canyoning.

interestGroups.title: French hill station
interestGroups.summary: The 1930s station, the last emperor’s villa, the pink churches, and Crazy House between lake mornings.

blocks.heading: Station, villa, and churches
paragraphs: The tourist railway is the art-deco run toward Trai Mat. Crazy House and Bao Dai Palace III fit between lake mornings. View the education college from the gate.

blocks.heading: The end of the line
paragraphs: Linh Phuoc is the mosaic pagoda at Trai Mat, often paired with the tourist train. It is not a French villa.

cards.title: Da Lat Railway Station
cards.summary: The 1930s art-deco station and the short tourist line toward Trai Mat.

cards.title: Bao Dai Palace III
cards.summary: The last emperor’s hill villa rooms and gardens south of the centre.

cards.title: Da Lat Cathedral
cards.summary: The pink cathedral and rooster-topped bell tower on Tran Phu.

cards.title: Domaine de Marie
cards.summary: Pink church and convent gardens on the west ridge.

cards.title: Education College
cards.summary: Curved colonnade and bell tower on Yersin. The view is from the gate.

cards.title: Crazy House
cards.summary: Dang Viet Nga’s surreal guesthouse you can walk through. Skip it if you only wanted the lake.

cards.title: Linh Phuoc
cards.summary: Mosaic pagoda at Trai Mat, often paired with the tourist train.

interestGroups.summary: Lam Vien Square is the lakeside stage for the December flower festival.
body: The 11th Flower Festival in 2026 opens at Lam Vien Square on 19 December and closes on 31 December, with displays into early January. Odd-year December is the pattern. Confirm the next year on arrival.
Displays that year are planned around Xuan Huong Lake. Road closures those nights are check on arrival. The ticketed city flower garden has no licensed photograph, so it is not a card.

cards.title: Lam Vien Square
cards.summary: Lakeside square, and the flower-festival opening and closing stage in December 2026.

interestGroups.title: Cool-evening stroll
interestGroups.summary: When the coast is still hot, the night market grills rice paper and the lake path stays lit.
body: After dark the night market lanes grill rice paper and pour hot soy milk. The shore of Xuan Huong stays lit. Bring a layer from November to January.

cards.title: Da Lat Market
cards.summary: Night stalls after 18:00, with grilled rice paper and soy milk. The sloping halls of flowers and strawberries are the morning in the same market.

cards.title: Xuan Huong at night
cards.summary: The lit lake path after the market. A walk or a pedal boat. Not the same outing as Tuyen Lam.

season.label: December to March
season.note: Vietnam Tourism names December to March as dry, cool, and sunny, with wild sunflowers on the hills in late autumn. Rain is concentrated May to October, and nights turn chilly November to January. Flower-festival displays in December 2026 are planned around Xuan Huong Lake; road closures those nights are check on arrival.

faqs.q: Can you combine Da Lat and Mui Ne?
faqs.a: They share a province after the merger and they are still a long ride apart. Fly or bus each one from Ho Chi Minh City rather than linking them in a day. Drive minutes are check on arrival.

faqs.q: How do you reach town from Lien Khuong Airport?
faqs.a: The airport is about 30 km south on Highway 20. Vietnam Tourism names flights from Ha Noi and Ho Chi Minh City. Taxi minutes and fares are check on arrival.
